_about: The approved product-facts manifest: the ONLY statements the content engine may make about Ollasync. Every fact points at where the public site or the shipped product states it (source). Change a fact here when the product changes; test/facts_drift.test.mjs re-derives the countable ones from src/data/*.ts and fails when they drift. Reviewed by a human before the engine's first run (2026-09-13).

facts.text: Live translation: while the trainer teaches, each learner can follow in their own language as live captions or as spoken audio. 19 languages are available.
One live class can run up to 5 different languages at the same time (learners choose individually).

The 19 languages are English, Spanish, French, Hindi, German, Chinese, Japanese, Portuguese, Arabic, Russian, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, Malayalam, Punjabi and Urdu; Arabic and Urdu are right-to-left. Each has a page at /languages/<code>/.
Live translation runs a beat behind the speaker, like listening through an interpreter; captions appear immediately and refine as the sentence completes.
It is machine translation of the trainer's live voice: excellent for following a lesson, not a substitute for a certified interpreter in legal or medical settings.

Numbers, IP addresses and port numbers come through as spoken in every language. Acronyms and product names written in Latin script are normally kept as they are, and a built-in technical vocabulary keeps common networking, software and cloud phrases in English instead of translating them in meaning. There is no guarantee for every arbitrary term.
facts.source: src/data/useCases.ts trainers FAQ; product voice rule shipped 2026-09-07 (19 languages, probe-proven); agents/translate-agent/vocab.py (per-session vocabulary, capped)

facts.text: Live captions: every participant can read real-time captions in the language they choose; captions and spoken translation are independent choices per person.
Learners join from a link in a modern browser on desktop or mobile; nothing to install and no account is required for invited guests. Trainers teach from the browser too.
The invitation email can carry a message written by the host (an optional invite note).
facts.source: src/data/useCases.ts trainers; dashboard invite-by-email note field (trainer tools, 2026-09-12)

facts.text: A class link is reusable across sessions and can carry a passcode; the passcode travels with the invitation and its calendar file.
facts.source: product: reusable /j/<room> link with passcode (shipped 2026-09-03), invitation .ics

facts.text: Every past session keeps its attendance — who joined — visible from the meeting's session history in the dashboard.
facts.source: src/data/useCases.ts trainers; dashboard Attendance per session (trainer tools, 2026-09-12)

facts.text: A wrap-up email can reach the host when a class ends; attendance and the wrap-up email are switches in the workspace settings (Settings › Trainer tools).
facts.source: src/data/useCases.ts trainers; dashboard Settings › Trainer tools

facts.text: AI class notes: a recorded class can be transcribed and summarised automatically (an opt-in switch); the notes give a summary, the key topics and action items.
facts.source: src/data/features.ts ai; dashboard auto-notes switch (trainer tools, 2026-09-12)

facts.text: From a recording, the host can send the AI notes to everyone on the invite list, or to typed addresses, in one step.
facts.source: src/data/useCases.ts trainers; dashboard Send notes (trainer tools, 2026-09-12)

facts.text: An assistant can be asked questions about any recorded class (summary, action items) from its transcript.
AI features are opt-in per workspace, run after the class on its recording, and never run on end-to-end encrypted meetings.
facts.source: src/data/features.ts ai (and the file's claim ceiling header); src/data/useCases.ts trainers compliance

facts.text: Recordings and their transcripts live in the workspace under access control: only people the host allows can open them, never a public link; retention is the host's choice (keep an archive or clear when a cohort ends).
Recording is explicit and visible to everyone in the class; there is no silent capture.
Local recording: a viewer can record the class on their own device, in the language they are listening to, with nothing uploaded to a server.

Webinars for large classes: a presenting stage and a view-only audience, moderated Q&A, polls and quizzes during the session, handouts attached to it, and a professional broadcast feed via OBS/RTMPS when wanted.
Video classes: HD video with screen sharing, a whiteboard, breakout rooms, background blur and full host controls.
Pricing is per trainer/staff seat; learners join sessions without a paid seat. It is free to start; the plans are on /pricing/.
A meeting can be end-to-end encrypted per meeting (optional). An encrypted class cannot be recorded, transcribed or summarised — that trade is deliberate.
facts.source: src/data/features.ts video-meetings (the file's claim ceiling header); src/pages/virtual-classroom-software.astro tradeoffs

facts.text: Data handling: encryption in transit, access control and audit logging are described on /security/, and a data-processing agreement is available (/dpa/). Ollasync holds no certification and says so.
Attendance, the wrap-up email, automatic notes, sending notes and the invite note are each a switch the host can turn on or off in workspace settings.
facts.source: dashboard Settings › Trainer tools (trainer tools v1, 2026-09-12)

facts.text: Ollasync is a cloud service used from the browser; it is not installed on the customer's own servers.
facts.source: src/data/features.ts video-meetings (the file's claim ceiling header: 100% cloud SaaS)

never: Never claim certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, 'HIPAA certified', 'GDPR certified', FedRAMP) — say 'controls and a DPA'.
Never say Ollasync is EU-hosted, self-hosted, on-premise or installable on the customer's servers.
Never name an integration (calendar, LMS, CRM, payment tool) — none is published.
Never state a latency figure, an uptime figure, a class-size number, a price in currency, a customer name, a quote, a testimonial, a case study or a market statistic.
Never name a language that is not in F03, a bigger language count than 19, or more than 5 languages per session.
Never describe AI features on end-to-end encrypted meetings.
Never mention the vendors, models or infrastructure behind the product; speak in capabilities and open standards (WebRTC, TLS).

Never describe how the product works internally — where translation, captions, recording or notes are processed (browser or server), how audio is routed, what the architecture does — beyond the exact wording of a fact. Describe what a trainer and a learner experience, not the mechanism.
Never state that a feature works in a situation a fact does not cover (for example anything about local recording or AI features during an end-to-end encrypted class beyond F19 and F23).
